anael.title: Lamplighter
anael.text:
At dusk, Anael walks the street with you and lights the lanterns. She does it by touching them. Each one blooms as her fingers leave it, and the row of flames follows the two of you down the hill. Her wings are folded neatly behind her.

She has been observing you for some weeks now. She tells you so, plainly, and she gives you her findings.

The Lantern Stone burned on the night you arrived, for the first time in four hundred years. Nobody lit it. She has examined the stone, the oil and the wick. She has interviewed the baker twice. She has gone through every other soul who came into Hollowmere that night and ruled each of them out.

"I have concluded that it was you," she says.

You tell her that's absurd. You run a pleasure house, and you apologize to chairs.

"I know." She gives you a small, helpless smile. "I have checked my reasoning several times, and I've run out of other explanations. I find I am not sorry."
ngpp: Even before her fingertip touches the brass wick, the streetlamp catches a faint ember and makes her wings twitch in brief puzzlement.
"Strange," Anael murmurs, pausing mid-stride. "The Lantern Stone has not merely sparked this evening—it answered me before I spoke your name."
Her golden eyes hold yours longer than duty allows. "My report says we only just met tonight, Sam. Yet every flame along this lane already knows your step beside mine."

choices.label: "I'm glad it was me."
choices.res: Her wings relax a full inch, pale primary feathers settling with a soft whisper against the stone wall. "So am I," Anael admits quietly, meeting your eyes without blinking once. "I find I am no longer at all objective about what happens under this roof." The next lantern wick lights on its own a fraction of a second before her fingertip even reaches the oil.

choices.label: Ask what happens when she finds out
choices.res: "I write a report," Anael says, her pale fingers hovering steadily above the cold wick of the next wall sconce while she weighs her own honesty. After a long pause, the corner of her mouth softens slightly. "Or perhaps I do not file it tonight. That particular paragraph of the Order's protocol has grown remarkably vague." The flint strikes cleanly, though the flame trembles like a held breath.

image.comp: walking along a street at dusk lighting lanterns with a touch of her fingertip, wings folded behind her, turning to him with a small smile

anael.title: Not the Wings
anael.text:
You open the washroom door, and Anael is sitting on the edge of the tub.

Her wings are soaked. They hang heavy on either side of her and drip steadily onto the tiles. She's wrapped in a towel, and she's blushing from her hairline to somewhere below the top of it. In the steam, her halo has dimmed to the glow of a single candle.

She has a comb in her hand and a look of defeat.

"The Order does not prepare one," she says, with enormous dignity, "for the maintenance of plumage. In the Quiet Lamp there are attendants who see to it." She draws one wing across in front of herself, like a shield. A good deal of water comes with it. "Do not touch the wings. It is impolite. It's considered rather intimate, among my kind."

She looks at the comb, and at the six feet of wet feathers she can't reach.

1.text:
You open the washroom door, and Anael is sitting on the rim of the bath with her feathers heavy from the steam. A deep blush runs down past her collarbone into the towel.

She doesn't raise a wing between you this time. She opens them a little, and her halo pulses a warm amber.

"It is still considered terribly improper," she whispers. She's shy about it, but she's looking at you, and she holds out a dry linen cloth. "I've been thinking about it since you offered. Among my kind one only allows it from someone one trusts completely. I would like your hands to be the ones that dry them."

choices.label: Kneel behind her and dry her wings slowly
choices.res: A shiver runs down every primary feather as your palms trace the warm curve of her wing-joint.

choices.label: Hand her the dry towel and step out gently
choices.res: "Thank you, Sam," she breathes, pressing the linen tightly to her glowing throat.

image.comp: perched on the rim of a tub in a towel, wings opened a little with halo glowing amber, shy blush, holding out a dry linen cloth

3.text:
You push the washroom door open. Anael is standing beside the steaming bath, ankle-deep in the first step of it. Her towel is already folded on the stool.

Halo-light spills gold across her bare tits and her hips and the long white sweep of her feathers. She turns to face you. She's trembling slightly, and she isn't ashamed. Her wings open just wide enough to make a space between them the size of you.

"Protocol left this house a long time ago," she says softly. "I've stopped pretending I miss it. Come into the water with me, Sam, and put your hands wherever you like."

choices.label: Step into the steam and draw her into the bath
choices.res: Warm white wings fold instinctively around your back as she pulls you down into the water with her.

choices.label: Kiss her bare shoulder and wash the soap from her feathers
choices.res: She leans back against your chest with a long, helpless sigh, her halo dimming to warm ember.

image.comp: standing ankle-deep beside the bath, bare body in golden halo-light, wings opened wide to make a space, trembling soft smile

choices.label: Apologize and back out
choices.res: "Thank you," Anael murmurs, lifting one wing swiftly to shield her shoulder while her halo brightens in sharp embarrassment. "For extending that courtesy. It is duly noted." That note, as it turns out, arrives beneath your office door later that same evening, written in calm, formal calligraphy—and carrying a single soft white feather pressed carefully between the pages.

choices.label: "Can I help dry them?"
choices.res: She stands remarkably still beneath your hands while you blot the warm dampness patiently down the curve of her feathers, letting out each breath carefully so she won't startle you. Every pass of warm linen across the base of her wing sends a small, unmistakable shiver straight down her spine—and when you finish, her halo burns brighter than all the brass lamps combined.

else.res: "No," she says, rigid, wing clutched tighter. "Please leave." The wings snap shut with a thump, and a few droplets scatter across your hoodie.

choices.label: Offer her the soap
choices.res: Anael takes the carved soap cake with both palms and turns it thoughtfully between long fingers, faintly perplexed by the scent of pressed mountain cedar. "We have never required earthly washing," she confesses softly, color warming the tips of her ears as she hides the bar inside her clean towel. Yet she keeps it anyway, and three days later you spot it resting proudly on her bedside sill.

image.comp: perched on the edge of a tub in a towel with dripping wings drawn in front of her like a shield, blushing hard

anael.title: Field Research: Pie
anael.text:
Anael has decided to try human food. She says it's research. Three hundred and eighty-nine years of tending lamps did not involve eating, and she feels that her notes on mortal life are incomplete.

The cook gives her a slice of berry pie.

She approaches it as if it might be a trap. She holds the fork like a surgical instrument. The afternoon light slants across her wings and across the plate, and she studies the pie from two angles before she commits.

After the first bite she goes completely still.

After the second, her halo flickers.

After the third she puts the fork down and looks you directly in the eye.

"This changes my understanding of mortality," she says gravely. "You have very little time, and you spend some of it on this. I think that's wise of you." There's a berry stain at the corner of her mouth. "Please do not tell the Order how much I enjoyed it."

choices.label: Stay with her
choices.res: You settle onto the wooden bench beside her and pull the plate between you. Anael cuts a neat wedge and holds the bite up to your lips as solemnly as though she were administering a quiet sacrament, her halo humming faintly above both your heads. Dark berry juice stains the corner of her lower lip when she tastes her share, and for once she leaves the smudge undisturbed.

choices.label: Thumb the berry stain off her lip and take her upstairs
choices.res: Her golden halo flares bright amber the very second your thumb glides across her berry-sweet lower lip. Anael catches her breath cleanly, leans into the warm brush of your knuckles without lowering her gaze, and murmurs that the dessert can finish upstairs before hooking her slender fingers squarely into the collar of your jacket.

choices.label: Order a second slice
choices.res: She accepts the fresh pastry with immaculate celestial dignity and an incline of her head worthy of an archivist receiving holy scripture. Five minutes later she clears that plate far faster than the first—licking sugar gently from her thumb before she catches you watching, and eyes the empty rim afterward as cleanly as though the porcelain had conspired to betray her.

image.comp: seated at a table with a slice of berry pie, eyes wide with solemn wonder, a soft glow flickering behind her head

anael.title: Recall
anael.text:
A second angel appears in the courtyard at noon. She's tall and stern, and the lamps flare white when she lands. She carries a scroll with the seal of the Quiet Lamp.

The Order has completed its review. Anael's reports have grown long and they have wandered from the point. Her superiors have noticed. She is recalled, and she's to present herself at the next new moon. Another Warden will be assigned to the case.

Anael takes the scroll with perfect composure. She thanks her sister, tucks it into her sleeve, and asks after the weather at home. The stern angel leaves in a rush of feathers.

Anael goes back to the bar and finishes polishing the glasses. She doesn't mention it at dinner.

That night you hear something in the corridor and open your door. She's standing outside it with her wings drooping and one hand raised to knock. From the look of her, she has been there a long while.

She hasn't knocked.
ngpp: Looking down at the red seal in the corridor, she shivers slightly, as though she has already heard herself refuse it once.
"I have not written the reply yet," she murmurs at your threshold, "and yet my hand remembers the exact line I mean to send."
"Four centuries of law," she whispers against your sleeve, wings trembling, "and all I can feel in my bones is how fiercely I chose your doorway over theirs before."

choices.label: "Go, if it's your duty."
choices.res: "Duty," Anael repeats softly to the quiet corridor, turning the heavy parchment word over like an unfamiliar coin. For the first time since she arrived beneath your roof, she sounds genuinely uncertain of what the word weighs. She does not pack her satchel, yet she leaves the Order's sealed dispatch unanswered on the mantel while her halo flickers thoughtfully in the dark.

choices.label: "Stay. Please."
choices.res: Anael unrolls a blank sheet against the stair rail, writes exactly one blunt line in crisp black ink, and reads her blunt refusal directly to the Order cleanly aloud without a trace of hesitation. The young winged messenger blinks rapidly, half scandalized and wholly unsure whether to salute or flee, beating his wings off the veranda before she even finishes turning scarlet from brow to collar.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.res: She stands motionless in the hall for five long heartbeats waiting for a hand on her sleeve that never moves, then folds the untouched dispatch slowly into neat thirds and inclines her head with flawless, distant courtesy. Her golden halo drops to a pale amber ember for days afterward, and every wall lantern along the front steps seems to burn a fraction lower.

image.comp: standing outside his door at night holding a sealed scroll, wings drooping, uncertain, halo dim
image.setting: dim inn corridor at night, moonlight through a window

anael.title: Evensong
anael.text:
There's a chapel nook at the back of the house, with a bench and a few candles. Nobody uses it much. Anael asks if you'd like to hear the evensong of her Order, and you say yes.

She sings it standing, with her hands folded. It's slow and very old. It's about lanterns set in windows, and the people who come home to them.

The candlelight shivers on her wings. Every flame in the room rises and falls with her voice.

You can't sing, and you never could. But there's a low line underneath the melody, and without deciding to, you start to hum it.

The lanterns brighten.

Anael stops in the middle of a verse and stares at you. Then she starts to laugh. It's bright and helpless, and her halo flares with it.

"They're answering you," she says. "They have only ever answered Wardens. What are you?" She's still laughing. "No. Don't stop. Do it again."

choices.label: Keep humming
choices.res: You stay right where you sit and keep humming quietly underneath her clear, silver phrasing until the old choir hymn carries all the way through its final verse—one voice luminous as cathedral glass and the other unapologetically flat against the floorboards. When the note fades out, Anael wipes real tears softly off her cheek and whispers that nobody has ever sung beside her like that before.

choices.label: Listen in silence
choices.res: You keep complete silence on the window bench while Anael tilts her head back, golden eyes shut gently in the dusk light, singing the entire forgotten hymn for an audience of one. Every clear phrase fills the small sitting room until the air feels warm against your palms—and for hours after her voice goes quiet, the timbers around you hold that gentle glow.

image.comp: standing in front of a small candlelit altar singing with wings half-spread, her halo glowing, glancing back at him with a delighted smile
image.setting: small candlelit chapel nook of an inn at night

anael.title: Report Withheld
anael.text:
Anael finds you on the roof, late. The whole sleeping town is laid out below you in lantern light, and she has just been around it lighting the last of them.

She sits down beside you. Then she opens her wings and folds them around you both. The feathers are warm, and softer than you'd have thought possible.

"The new moon is in three days," she says. "I've written my final report. I was asked to determine whether this soul is a danger to the world."

She takes the scroll out of her sleeve and shows you. It's one line long.

"I find that he's a danger only to my composure. I have recommended no further action." She meets your eyes, golden and brave. "I'm not sending it, and I'm not going back. I have tended other people's lamps for a very long time. I would like to stay, Sam. Not as a Warden. As yours."

Downstairs, your door closes behind you both.
ngpp: As her wings gather warmth around your shoulders, a sudden stillness crosses her face, as though this starlit sanctuary already knew your names.
"The Lantern Stone burned twice as bright tonight," she whispers against your temple, halo soft as candlelight. "Almost as if it remembered how this night ends."
"Every memory swept clean," Anael murmurs, golden eyes shimmering as her wings lock around you, "yet my feathers still remember every shiver of yours, Sam. Choose me again."
anael.goLead: You take Anael's hand and lead her down the attic stair to your bed. Her white wings spread wide across the pillows, and by candlelight she lets go of the last of her vows.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Anael inclines her bright head smoothly, not a hint of disappointment dimming the steady golden band circling her crown. "I can wait," she murmurs softly, resting warm fingers across the back of your wrist before drawing away. "The Order measures devotion in whole centuries, Sam. Only do not keep me waiting quite as long as that—I have grown fond of earthly impatience."
